_note: Member-specific values. Scripts read it through scripts/config.py; pages read member, leader and profile through site.js. Fields starting with TODO must be filled before the step that needs them.

fec._leadersNote: leaders.<chamber> lists the party leaders whose committees' money build_establishment.py totals per cycle (chamber = member.chamber). A gift counts when the giving committee's FEC ID is in 'ids' or its name matches 'rx' (name-only matches are printed for checking). 'numKey' exposes a leader's all-cycle total to establishment_items.json as {dccc} or {dscc}. leadershipRx/leadershipIds drive the Money page's single-leader box: House 'JEFFRIES|JEFF PAC'; Senate 'SCHUMER|^IMPACT$' with leadershipIds ["C00346312", "C00348607"].

senate.title: Senate Republican leadership and Trump
senate.note: Contributions from each Senate Republican leader's campaign committee, leadership PAC and joint fundraising committees, from the NRSC, and from President Trump's committees, from FEC filings. Committees are matched by FEC committee ID. Super PACs such as the Senate Leadership Fund cannot give to candidates; their independent spending is not counted here.
senate._source: Committee IDs: FEC API /candidate/<id>/committees/, /committees/?sponsor_candidate_id= and /committees/?q= (cycles 2024 and 2026), read 2026-11-27; each leader's 'src' links the FEC committee pages. Roles (Thune leader, Barrasso whip, Cotton conference chair) are from memory of the 119th Congress and NOT yet confirmed on senate.gov (blocked from the cloud): confirm at https://www.senate.gov/senators/leadership.htm, and add Capito, Lankford or others if wanted. Trump committee IDs copied from the House Republican block.

fec._cyclesNote: cycles are FEC two-year periods named by their even end year. House: the first race and the current cycle. Senate (six-year terms): resolve_fec.py writes the election cycle that began the current term through the current cycle, e.g. Padilla (elected 2022) 2022, 2024, 2026; Schiff (elected 2024) 2024, 2026. Every build script loops over this list.

geo._note: Senators have no district map: fetch_geo.py and build_map.py are House-only, and index.html hides the map.

statements._note: localTerms: |-separated place names that mark a release as local news (lowercase).

overview._note: Member-specific Overview tiles (scripts/build_overview.py). costPromise: start of the promise 'issue' in data/promises.json whose status answers 'Delivering on cost of living?'. themes: [{q, rx, section, noun}] counts press releases mentioning a topic (e.g. Luz Rivas: Focused on homelessness?). votes: [{q, roll, section, what}] shows one recorded vote (e.g. the Epstein Files Transparency Act, House roll 2025-289).

_peersNote: Members to compare with on the Overview and Money pages: {id, name, dist, group}. id is the vote id (bioguide for the House, LIS id for the Senate). Groups appear in config order; the build counts 'Party leadership', 'Centrist' and 'Progressive' in its summary.

profile._note: Curated page text, rendered by the pages at runtime. Strings allow [label](url), **bold** and {{tokens}} (e.g. {{short}}, {{poss}}). Every fact typed here also goes in data/claims_static.json with its source.

state._note: Optional statewide context shown in place of the House district map; hidden while intro and facts are empty.
